short: The first tank with a fully rotating turret, the layout every tank has used since.
full:
Designed by Louis Renault and Rodolphe Ernst-Metzmaier at the urging of General Jean-Baptiste Estienne, the FT was tested in prototype form in early 1917 and reached the front the following year. It weighed under seven tonnes and carried a crew of two: a driver low in the front, and a commander who also loaded and fired the gun from a turret mounted on a ball race that turned through a full circle, with the engine behind a bulkhead at the rear. Its combat debut came on 31 May 1918 in the Forest of Retz, supporting Moroccan infantry against the German spring offensive.

France chose to build it in quantity rather than pursue heavy tanks, producing roughly 3,700 by the armistice; the United States built its own version as the M1917. Exported widely, FTs fought in Spain, China and Poland, and were still on the French inventory when Germany invaded in 1940. Its arrangement of driver, turret and rear engine became the standard tank layout.
